The test image shows a corn ear with dark green/teal mold heavily coating the kernels. The mold appears dense and covers most of the ear surface. This is a seed/pod affected part.

Let me read the part index and then check reference images for the top candidates.

The test image is an ear/pod with dense dark green/teal mold on kernels. Part index narrows to: pod (7 classes) and seed (8 classes). Top candidates: **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** and **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**.

Let me view one reference from each of 8 different classes:

The Trichoderma seed reference is an excellent visual match to the test image: yellow/orange kernels with dark blue-green/teal mold growing between and on them, with the same dense, patchy coverage pattern.

Summary of comparisons:
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (seed): nearly identical — dark teal/blue-green mold on yellow kernels, same distribution
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: olive-gray powdery mold, concentrated at tip — different color and pattern
- **Gibberella_Disease**: pink/red mold — clearly different color
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: white mold from base — wrong color
- **Head_Smut**: brown spore masses replacing ear structure — very different
- **Fusarium_Disease**: white/pinkish patchy mold — wrong color
- **Common_Smut**: large white/black galls — very different morphology

The test image matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot seed reference almost exactly.
